J_state_partition.semantic_rule: Fork semantics cover every mutable byte capable of changing either branch's future integer probabilities. An implementation may use copy-on-write files, sparse journals, or recomputation only if the independent state-access manifest proves semantic identity to a complete fork.
J_state_partition.shareable_state: Truth-only state may be shared only after a source audit proves its transition is arm-invariant and free of writable aliases into branch-dependent state.
J_state_partition.forked_state: Every parameter, optimizer moment, recurrent value, mixer or SSE value, context value, cache, cursor, schedule value, or other mutable state whose transition depends on a branch probability, loss, or F write is branch-local.
J_state_partition.coder_rule: The arithmetic coder is never forked or rewound. J codes only the adapted branch probabilities during bytes 32 through 63 and continues its resulting interval across the rejoin.
J_state_partition.join_rule: At the boundary after byte 63, retain the untouched parent branch state exactly, discard every adapted branch write, retain the continuous coder state, and begin the next prediction from the retained parent branch.

required_identity_proofs: P and J's untouched parent branch consume identical truths and execute ordinary updates at identical native call sites and cadence.
F and J's adapted branch have identical midpoint inputs, update writes, rebuilt state, second-half integer probabilities, and second-half post-truth transitions through byte 63.
The retained J parent branch state equals the independently continued P state at every byte-64 join boundary.
No adapted parameter, optimizer, recurrent, mixer, SSE, context, memory, cache, cursor, schedule, or other probability-affecting write survives J rejoin.
Encode, repeat encode, decode, and raw inverse agree for every arm.
